node.title: Re^4: backticks and system()
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
One last question though. How do you know about all these rules and problems that they come up on all these commands?

Mostly it was a detailed reading of [doc://system], [doc://exec], [doc://open], [doc://perlop#qx/_STRING_/|qx// in perlop], the relevant parts of [doc://perlipc], [man://execvp;3|execvp(3)], a few bits from [doc://perlport], as well as posts such as [afoken]'s [id://1205217] and e.g. [id://1199200|this one] by [salva], plus some additional information that was linked to from those docs. I also recall testing things out with e.g. [man://strace] and looking at the various modules' code while writing [id://1180578|this node].

Correct me if I am wrong, but qw explicitly converts the strings inside the parenthesis to a list of strings right? I am confused about this part. If I come across a similar case I should explicitly define the list of commands or I can use qw?

Yes, basically qw// splits on whitespace, so the two forms you showed in your node "my @args = qw(Runbatch.exe -j dpsgl -r dpstst);" and "my @args = ('Runbatch.exe', '-j', 'dpsgl', '-r', 'dpstst');" are identical and the "Not Recommended" / "Recommended" doesn't really apply.

Note that qw// has nothing to do with qx//, they are two completely different operators that just happen to have similar names. qx// treats its argument as a single string, and you get the whitespace handling from the shell, so the same thing that happens at the command line when you type a command - this also means that whitespace can be quoted*, e.g. qx/echo "foo bar"/ is exactly like typing echo "foo bar" at the command prompt and would pass a single string "foo bar" to the command echo (assuming a "normal" shell). qw// just splits on whitespace, regardless of any quoting - qw/echo "foo bar"/ returns a list of three elements, ('echo', '"foo', 'bar"'). See also [doc://perlop#Quote-Like-Operators]. Therefore, in e.g. system(qw/echo "foo bar"/), the shell would be avoided because [doc://system] was passed more than one argument, and the echo command would receive two arguments instead of one.

* However, getting that quoting right can get very complicated if there are special characters in the strings, which is why modules like [mod://ShellQuote::Any] are a better approach, or, IMHO even better, just avoid the shell in the first place.
